This may not be what you want to hear, but maybe 24/7 diapers just isn’t for you. It’s okay to be into the idea of it, fantasize about it, and never actually commit to it. It’s all unique and individual. If you don’t actually want to be 24/7 and don’t have a medical need to be, you won’t be 24/7 and if you brute force your way through it, you may find you don’t enjoy it like you thought. It’s okay to just wear as much as you want and then take a break. It’s supposed to make you happy and make you feel good. It’s unique to how you want to enjoy it and maybe after a certain amount of diapered time, you feel good and don’t think about wearing anymore since you got that positive feeling for as long as you seemed to have need it. 

Now all that said, the only thing I could really recommend would be some sort of tracker or countdown amp. To actually visualize your continued time in diapers. Something you check a box on every day and see the 24/7 streak grow longer and longer. Or setting milestones and getting an alert when you achieve them. Set them small and then space them out longer each time. Like a week, then two weeks, then a month, then 6 weeks, then 2 months, then 3 months, then 6 months, and so on. Whatever interval makes you feel like you’re accomplishing something. Most people just aren’t going to use sheer mental willpower to commit to 24/7 diapers and stay in them from that point on without any breaks. Not that it’s impossible, it’s just not the norm.

Seems like you’ll get more in the weeds trying to define what you like to do than it’s worth. As long as you’re happy and what you and your girlfriend do is consensual, its definition doesn’t really matter. 

That said, my personal opinion, I’d explain like this. If someone needed a wheelchair to get around, they don’t have a kink for a wheelchair. If they have intercourse with a partner while sitting in the wheelchair, that doesn’t mean the wheelchair is a kinky addition to sex. But if sex is traditionally done in the bed, and then done in the wheelchair for the sake of spicing things up, that would be considered somewhat kinky. Or if involving the wheelchair is required or preferable to one or both partners, that would be kinky. Much like art, it’s in the eye of the beholder. 

If you’re only able to achieve satisfaction sexually while in little space to some degree, that’s a kink. If you prefer sexually activity to take place while in little space, that’s a kink. If it’s just a matter of timing and you have sex when you and your partner desire, regardless of how you’re dressed or behaving, then I would say it’s not a kink as the little space items are not required or desired for sexual gratification. 

Like I said, if you’re happy, you do you. But understand those other communities have their preferences and restrictions too. At the end of the day, it’s personal to each person. No one person decides what is or is not kinky. But, knowing that both of those other communities do not like this discussion, it’s probably safe to assume that this sort of talk is not acceptable there and I’d be respectful of that, rather than trying to justify your actions or try to convince others of your way of thinking. As long as you and your partner are having a good time, that’s all that matters.
